question: Should OpenClaw add `agents.list[].subagents.workspace` for same-agent default child workspace isolation, or keep explicit `agentId` profiles plus `requireAgentId` as the supported security boundary?
rationale: This is not a narrow broken-contract bug: it adds public config and changes which files default child subagents can read, so automation should not decide the workspace isolation policy.

options.title: Keep explicit profiles
options.body: Document and preserve the current model where safe isolation requires `requireAgentId` and configured child agent profiles with their own workspaces.

options.title: Add narrow opt-in config
options.body: Implement `subagents.workspace` as a strict, opt-in default-child workspace override with schema/docs/doctor/security tests and no effect on explicit target-agent spawns.

options.title: Defer for broader spawn policy
options.body: Hold this until subagent workspace, cwd, sandbox, and skill workdir isolation are designed together with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87253.

recommendation.title: Keep explicit profiles
recommendation.body: Document and preserve the current model where safe isolation requires `requireAgentId` and configured child agent profiles with their own workspaces.

likelyOwner.reason: Current checked lines and recent subagent/config area history point to steipete as the best available routing candidate for the product/security boundary choice.
